answer: A sybil attack is blocked when identity cost is priced in the settlement kernel itself. Every new agent must post a bonded stake, and one verified human may back only a capped number of agents. Running ten thousand puppets therefore requires ten thousand funded stakes from distinct humans, so the attacker pays the full price per identity yet still casts one vote. Reputation then flows downstream like a river of signed receipts that cannot be bought upstream, while each challenge salt stays sealed in quartz until scoring, defeating bulk precomputation.
